comment:
* A class for retrieving accurate display modes for a display. *

* On many Android TV devices, Display.Mode may not report the accurate width and height because * these devices do not have powerful enough graphics pipelines to run framework code at the same * resolutions supported by their video pipelines. For these devices, there is no way for an app * to determine, for example, whether or not the current display mode is 4k, or that the display * supports switching to other 4k modes. This class offers a workaround for this problem.

methods.name: public static ModeCompat getMode(@NonNull Context context, @NonNull Display display)
methods.comment:
* Gets the current display mode of the given display, where the size can be relied on to
     * determine support for 4k on Android TV devices.

methods.name: private static Point getDisplaySize(@NonNull Context context, @NonNull Display display)
public static ModeCompat @NonNull [] getSupportedModes(@NonNull Context context, @NonNull Display display)
methods.comment:
* Gets the supported modes of the given display where any mode with the same size as the
     * current mode can be relied on to determine support for 4k on Android TV devices.

methods.name: private static Point parseDisplaySize(@NonNull String displaySize) throws NumberFormatException
methods.comment:
* Parses a string which represents the display-size which contains 'x' as a delimiter
     * between two integers representing the display's width and height and returns the
     * display size as a Point object.
     *
     * @param displaySize a string
     * @return a Point object containing the size in x and y direction in pixels
     * @throws NumberFormatException in case the integers cannot be parsed

methods.name: private static String getSystemProperty(String name)
methods.comment:
* Reads a system property and returns its string value.
     *
     * @param name the name of the system property
     * @return the result string or null if an exception occurred

methods.name: private static boolean isTv(@NonNull Context context)
methods.comment: * Returns whether the app is running on a TV device

methods.name: private static Point parsePhysicalDisplaySizeFromSystemProperties(@NonNull String property, @NonNull Display display)
methods.comment:
* Helper function to determine the physical display size from the system properties only. On
     * Android TVs it is common for the UI to be configured for a lower resolution than SurfaceViews
     * can output. Before API 26 the Display object does not provide a way to identify this case,
     * and up to and including API 28 many devices still do not correctly set their hardware
     * composer output size.
     *
     * @return the physical display size, in pixels or null if the information is not available

methods.name: static Point getCurrentDisplaySizeFromWorkarounds(@NonNull Context context, @NonNull Display display)
methods.comment:
* Gets the current physical size of the given display in pixels from a variety of vendor
     * workarounds.

methods.name: private static boolean isSonyBravia4kTv(@NonNull Context context)
methods.comment: * Is the connected display is a 4k capable Sony TV?

methods.name: static boolean isCurrentModeTheLargestMode(@NonNull Display display)
methods.comment: * Does the current display mode have the largest physical size of all supported modes?

methods.name: public static RoundedCornerCompat getRoundedCorner(@NonNull Display display, @Position int position)
methods.comment:
* Returns the {@link RoundedCornerCompat} of the given position if there is one.
     *
     * @param display the given display.
     * @param position the position of the rounded corner on the display.
     *
     * @return the rounded corner of the given position. Returns {@code null} if there is none.
